Video Games Are Too Dangerous for Voice Over Actors

After recently linking an article about the strike of (some of the) video game voice actors, I thought I might also share this one - given the source, it's naturally rather biased, but I think it does have a point in that voice acting for video games puts a lot more strain on the vocal chords of the actors than conventional acting does, whatnot with various death screams, pained grunts, or creature growls.

To give you an idea - the Hivemind in DoW2:Retribution? That gurgling mess of a voice? Lani Minella (otherwise known as Rouge the Bat for Sonic and Ivy Valentine in Soul Calibur) does that one.

and I generally like to avoid or negotiate limits on such request.

This is because of one of two things.

A: they're being little bitches, saying that having to scream, or yell AS A VOICE ACTOR causes them physical pain, which means they're shitty voice actors.

B: they want more pay, and they're being little bitches about it.

Yeah, no.

Excessive yelling and screaming is extremely detrimental to your vocal cords. Developing nodes on your chords is at best the end of your career as a voice actor, at worst handicapping your ability to speak up for the rest of your life.

The issue isn't that they are screaming, it's that one person is being expected to voice 5-10 different people or creatures screaming or yelling in a single session. Ten minutes of dialog can take more than an hour to record.

Imagine you're being paid to scream into a microphone. You give the producer 10 different screams at the top of your lungs. He only likes 2 of them, and now you have to do 8 more to fill his quota. This repeats ad nauseam until you've been screaming more or less constantly for two straight hours.

You can't ask for a break because they only booked 4 hours in the studio and you still have 5 monster growls, 7 different versions of generic guard dialog, and 2 paragraphs of a monologue for the main villain to say.

Ask anybody who uses their voice for a living, whether it's voice acting, professional singers, announcers, whatever. You have to take very good care of your voice in order to keep it up at that level. The lawsuit is being raised because the game companies do not understand this, seeing as lots of voice acting in games is a relatively new trend. Of course the actors have to scream in other media. But they are given warning, breaks, and additional "hazard" pay for strenuous work as such.
